column2: Computer Science and Information Technology Society
column5: The Computer Science and Information Technology (CSIT) Society is dedicated to fostering professional and technical growth for students in computing, software, and IT. We bring together like-minded individuals to collaborate, learn, and connect with the tech industry.

We are the RMIT Information Security Collective (RISC), a student-run group passionate about cybersecurity. We run workshops, talks, and CTFs to help each other build skills in ethical hacking, cyber defense, and everything in between. Everyone’s welcome, no matter your experience level. Welcome to the RMIT Information Security Collective!
Founded in 2012, RISC was established to bridge the gap between academia and industry in cybersecurity by creating opportunities for students to explore, share, and develop their skills through hands-on learning and community involvement. The club hosts a variety of student-led events ranging from technical workshops to social activities designed to support students of all experience levels. In addition to building technical skills, RISC promotes cybersecurity awareness on campus and facilitates meaningful connections with peers, alumni, and industry professionals.

RMIT Electrical, Electronic & Computer Engineering (REECE) is a student-led society committed to enriching the academic and professional journey of students in electrical, electronic and computer engineering at RMIT. Our mission is to connect students with industry, foster hands-on technical skills and build a strong peer network.

We host a range of events including industry panels, technical workshops, site visits and social meetups all designed to help students bridge the gap between theory and practice, and explore emerging trends in engineering and technology.

Whether you are looking to expand your knowledge, grow your network, or collaborate on innovative projects, REECE is here to support your development and help shape your future in engineering. 

Our sectors of focus include, Electrical, Electronic and Computer Engineering, Power and Control Systems Engineering, Telecommunications and Network Engineering, Embedded Systems and ASM, C/C++

RMIT Matrix is a club for Competitive Programming & Algorithms. We solve algorithmic problems, train for contests like ICPC, and get sharper together, whatever your starting point.  No competitive background needed.
MATRIX is open to every RMIT student. Plenty of us started knowing nothing about competitive programming.  What matters is the curiosity to pick apart a hard problem and the patience to learn the techniques. Beginners are genuinely welcome.

We are affiliated with the RMIT University Student Union (RUSU) and run by a volunteer committee. We focus on algorithmic problem-solving and contest training, a niche the general CS clubs do not fill.
RMIT Society for Women in Information TeCHnology (SWITCH) is open to all who are passionate in supporting diversity within Information Technology.
